question:
**Fill in the blank: **

The sacred masked dances performed by monks at Hemis represent various _____ of the Drugpa lineage.
solution:
The correct answer is __**guardian divinities**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• The sacred masked dances performed at the Hemis Monastery are known as Cham dances and are integral to the Buddhist festivals celebrated in Ladakh.

• These dances symbolize various **guardian divinities** of the Drugpa lineage, who are believed to protect the Buddhist teachings and practitioners.

• The guardian divinities are often depicted in elaborate masks and costumes, showcasing their wrathful and protective nature in Buddhist iconography.

• These performances are deeply spiritual and are conducted as a form of meditation and ritual to ward off negative energies and invoke blessings.

• The Hemis Festival, celebrated annually at the Hemis Monastery, is dedicated to Lord Padmasambhava, a major figure in Tibetan Buddhism, and features these sacred dances.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Reincarnated Lamas**

• Reincarnated lamas, also known as tulkus, are spiritual leaders believed to be the rebirths of enlightened beings or teachers in Tibetan Buddhism.

• These individuals play a pivotal role in guiding and preserving Buddhist teachings, but they are not directly related to the Cham dances at Hemis.

• Examples include the Dalai Lama and Panchen Lama, who are significant figures in Tibetan Buddhism.

• **Ancient Kings**

• Ancient kings, while often revered in cultural and historical contexts, are not the focus of the sacred dances performed at Hemis.

• The dances are more centered around spiritual themes like divinities, protection, and enlightenment rather than historical figures.

• However, Tibetan and Ladakhi history do include stories of kings who supported Buddhism, such as King Songtsen Gampo of Tibet.

• **Ancestral Spirits**

• Ancestral spirits are often venerated in various cultures and religions, including shamanistic practices, but they do not play a role in the Cham dances at Hemis.

• Buddhist rituals at Hemis focus on deities and divinities rather than ancestral spirits.

• The concept of spirits in Buddhism is more aligned with karmic cycles and the realms of existence rather than familial ancestors.

• **Main Theme: Drugpa Lineage and Cham Dance**

• The Drugpa lineage is one of the major schools of Tibetan Buddhism, known for its emphasis on tantric practices and meditation.

• The Cham dances are a significant part of Buddhist rituals, representing stories and teachings through symbolic movements and masks.

• These dances are performed to honor protector deities, ensure the spiritual welfare of the community, and celebrate the teachings of Buddhism.
